use: The sting of losing or being beaten when you could have won; English has no single word for it.

example.romaji: Ato chotto de kateta noni. Kuyashii!
example.ja: あとちょっとで勝てたのに。悔しい！

examplePolite.romaji: Ato chotto de kateta noni. Kuyashii desu.
examplePolite.ja: あとちょっとで勝てたのに。悔しいです。
examplePolite.english: We almost won. It's really frustrating.

notes: Not regret over your own wrongdoing; that's koukai.

use: Said straight to someone, friendly not bitter: 'ii na, urayamashii!' = lucky you!

example.ja: ハワイ行くの？うらやましい！
example.english: You're going to Hawaii? I'm so jealous!

examplePolite.romaji: Hawai ni iku n desu ka. Urayamashii desu.
examplePolite.ja: ハワイに行くんですか。うらやましいです。
examplePolite.english: You're going to Hawaii? I'm jealous.

notes: Slang short form: urayama. Shitto is the darker, possessive jealousy.

use: Often aimed at yourself: 'nasakenai' = I'm so pathetic.

example.romaji: Konna koto de naku nante, nasakenai na.
example.ja: こんなことで泣くなんて、情けないな。
example.english: Crying over something like this. How pathetic of me.

examplePolite.romaji: Konna koto de naku nante, nasakenai desu.
examplePolite.ja: こんなことで泣くなんて、情けないです。
examplePolite.english: Crying over something like this. It's pathetic of me.

notes: Stronger than hazukashii (embarrassed): it's disappointment in weakness.

english: so close!; a shame; a waste
use: Shouted when someone just misses: 'oshii!' = so close!

example.ja: 惜しい！ほぼ合ってるけど、違う。
example.english: So close! Nearly right, but no.

examplePolite.romaji: Oshii desu! Hobo atte imasu kedo, chigaimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 惜しいです！ほぼ合っていますけど、違います。
examplePolite.english: So close! Nearly right, but not quite.

notes: Also for losing something good: yameru no wa oshii = it's a shame to quit. Mottainai is the word for wasting things.

use: Says something doesn't bother or hurt you: 'heiki, heiki' = I'm fine, no problem.

examplePolite.ja: これぐらい平気ですよ。

notes: Close to daijoubu, but more 'it doesn't get to me'. Heiki de uso o tsuku = lie without a second thought.

english: much appreciated; a big help; grateful
use: Says something helps you: 'sore wa arigatai' = that would really help.

example.ja: 手伝ってくれるの？ありがたい！
example.english: You'll help me? That's a huge help!

examplePolite.romaji: Tetsudatte itadakeru n desu ka. Arigatai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 手伝っていただけるんですか。ありがたいです。
examplePolite.english: You'll help me? I really appreciate it.

notes: Arigatou comes from it: arigatai describes the help, arigatou is the thanks you say.

use: Social awkwardness: silence after a fight, running into an ex.

example.romaji: Kenka shita bakari dakara, kimazui na.
example.ja: けんかしたばかりだから、気まずいな。
example.english: We just had a fight, so it's awkward.

examplePolite.romaji: Kenka shita bakari na node, kimazui desu.
examplePolite.ja: けんかしたばかりなので、気まずいです。
examplePolite.english: We just had a fight, so it's awkward.

use: Hard-working and rule-following; can also mean a bit too straight-laced.

example.romaji: Kare, honto ni majime da yo ne.
example.ja: 彼、ほんとにまじめだよね。

examplePolite.romaji: Kare wa hontou ni majime desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は本当にまじめですね。

notes: Majime ni kotaete = answer me seriously. Majime is a personality; shinken is the attitude in the moment.

use: In speech it mostly means careless or whatever-works: 'tekitou ni yatta' = I just winged it.

example.romaji: Kare no henji, itsumo tekitou da yo ne.
example.ja: 彼の返事、いつも適当だよね。

examplePolite.romaji: Kare no henji wa itsumo tekitou desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 彼の返事はいつも適当ですね。

notes: The written sense 'suitable' survives in tekitou ni suwatte = sit wherever you like.

use: Fully serious about something right now: 'shinken ni kangaete' = think about it seriously.

example.romaji: Shinken ni hanashiteru n da kedo.
example.ja: 真剣に話してるんだけど。

examplePolite.romaji: Shinken ni hanashite iru n desu kedo.
examplePolite.ja: 真剣に話しているんですけど。

notes: Shinken na kao = a serious face.

english: sloppy; irresponsible; (iikagen ni shite) enough already
use: Iikagen na hito = someone you can't rely on; 'iikagen ni shite!' = knock it off!

example.ja: もう、いいかげんにしてよ！
example.english: Come on, knock it off already!

examplePolite.ja: もう、いいかげんにしてください。

notes: Close to tekitou, but more blaming. Iikagen na shigoto = sloppy work.

use: For strict people (parents, coaches) and tough conditions: 'kibishii na' = that's tough.

example.romaji: Uchi no oya, kekkou kibishii n da yo.
example.ja: うちの親、けっこう厳しいんだよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Uchi no oya wa kekkou kibishii n desu.
examplePolite.ja: うちの親はけっこう厳しいんです。

notes: Also for tight time or money: jikanteki ni kibishii = time is tight.

use: Someone who insists on getting their own way, like a spoiled child.

example.ja: もう、わがままばっかり言わないで。
example.english: Come on, stop being so demanding.

examplePolite.ja: あまりわがままを言わないでください。

notes: Wagamama o iu = make selfish demands. Also humble: wagamama itte sumimasen = sorry to ask for something special.

use: The protest 'zurui!' when someone gets something you don't, or cheats; often half-joking.

example.romaji: Hitori de zenbu tabeta no? Zurui!
example.ja: 一人で全部食べたの？ずるい！
example.english: You ate it all by yourself? No fair!

examplePolite.romaji: Hitori de zenbu tabeta n desu ka. Zurui desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 一人で全部食べたんですか。ずるいですよ。
examplePolite.english: You ate it all by yourself? That's not fair.

notes: Zurui hito = a sly, sneaky person.

use: Deliberately unkind, often in small ways; also playful: 'ijiwaru!' = you meanie!

example.ja: そんな意地悪言わないでよ。

examplePolite.ja: そんな意地悪を言わないでください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't say such mean things.

notes: Ijiwaru suru = be mean to, tease. Ijimeru is harsher: real bullying.
